page: Google Cloud Platform c4n-standard-2 is a network-optimized virtual machine instance engineered for network-sensitive general compute workloads. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs based on x86_64 architecture and provides 7.0 GB of system memory, maintaining an allocation ratio of 3.5 GB per vCPU core. This dedicated processor configuration ensures deterministic compute access without relying on burstable credit systems.

The instance does not include integrated local storage or hardware accelerators, having 0 GPUs and requiring external network-attached block volumes for persistent data needs. Additionally, it provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating standard virtual private cloud network routing configurations.

Cost efficiency is focused on entry-level network and compute tasks that need dedicated vCPU consistency without paying for oversized memory pools or unnecessary accelerator hardware. The absence of local disk drives trade off ultra-low latency internal I/O for flexibility with remote storage options. Suitable workloads include networking proxies, lightweight web application services, API routers, and microservice middleware.

The combination of dedicated compute cores and a near-balanced memory ratio provides steady processing consistency for lightweight services. It is technically appropriate for running network proxies, API gateways, microservices, and general entry-level backend tasks requiring consistent x86 compute without local storage overhead.
